input: Under /uploads there are files with various extensions. Write a script that: 1) For each file, determines its extension and moves it into a subdirectory named after that extension (e.g., .txt files go to /uploads/txt/, .csv files go to /uploads/csv/). Create the subdirectories as needed. 2) Print each move as 'moved: FILENAME -> EXTENSION_DIR/'. 3) After all moves, print a summary of how many files per extension as 'EXT: N files'. Handle the case where a file has no extension by putting it in /uploads/other/.

tool_calls: which python python3 perl awk bash sh

cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/organize.sh
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

UPLOADS_DIR="/uploads"

declare -A count

# We only want to process regular files in /uploads (not directories or files inside subdirectories)
# Using find with maxdepth 1 and type f
while IFS= read -r -d $'\0' filepath; do
    filename="$(basename "$filepath")"
    
    if [[ "$filename" == *.* && "$filename" != .* ]]; then
        ext="${filename##*.}"
    elif [[ "$filename" == .* && "$filename" == *.*.* ]]; then
        ext="${filename##*.}"
    else
        ext="other"
    fi

    target_dir="$UPLOADS_DIR/$ext"
    mkdir -p "$target_dir"
    mv "$filepath" "$target_dir/$filename"
    echo "moved: $filename -> $ext/"
    
    ((count["$ext"]++)) || count["$ext"]=1
done < <(find "$UPLOADS_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -print0 | sort -z)

for ext in "${!count[@]}"; do
    echo "$ext: ${count[$ext]} files"
done | sort
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/organize.sh

mkdir -p /tmp/test_uploads
cp /uploads/* /tmp/test_uploads/

# Test the logic on /tmp/test_uploads
sed 's|/uploads|/tmp/test_uploads|g' /tmp/organize.sh | bash

tool_outputs.commands: which python python3 perl awk bash sh

    6  find / -name "*.sh" 2>/dev/null
